bibliography.title: An effective strategy to enhance phosphoric acid retention and proton  conductivity stability: Construction of proton transfer channels with starch  rather than H 3 PO 4
bibliography.authors: Based on the results in this study and the Grotthuss proton transfer mechanism, dense hydrogen-bonds from  oxygen-containing groups in polymer backbones should be more stable than hydrogen-bonds from massive  H 3 PO 4  molecules with high acid doping levels to promote proton conduction.

mechanism_relevant_findings: The proton transfer channels are constructed through dense hydrogen bonds from the polymer backbones, promoting proton conduction.
limitations: Phosphoric acid (PA) leaching and mechanical stability remain concerns for high doping levels.

relevance_judgement.reason: The study provides insights into mechanisms and stability of proton conduction in composite membranes.
